WASHINGTON: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has recently moved from his Washington, DC residence to a US military base after Iranian threats against his life, two people familiar with the matter said on Tuesday (Nov 10). The New York Times first reported the move. A senior intelligence official in the Trump administration warned in a memo seen by Reuters late last month that Iranian plots against US personnel and American citizens had reached an advanced stage. Bessent has led the US sanctions and economic pressure campaign against Iran, dubbed Operation Economic Outcast, since August to try to push Tehran to end attacks on shipping and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The crucial waterway has been largely closed since the US and Israel attacked Iran on Feb 28. The economic pressure campaign, which coincides with a US naval blockade of Iranian ports, has included sanctions on Middle Eastern bank branches and other financial services firms facilitating transactions with Iran.

A source familiar with the matter said security concerns surrounding Bessent increased when the Wall Street Journal published an aerial view of the Georgetown mansion that Bessent bought for US$12.5 million shortly after his confirmation as Treasury secretary in January 2025. The photo allowed Bessent's home to be geolocated, and Bessent was relocated to a military base for his safety, the source said, adding: "The news media has an obligation to act responsibly amid growing threats against public officials." Iran has previously denied plotting to attack officials and people on US soil. item.title: ベセント米財務長官、軍基地に転居 イランの脅迫受け＝関係筋
item.description:
David Lawder Kanishka Singh
[ワシントン １０日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
David Lawder　Kanishka Singh

[ワシントン １０日 ロイター] - ベセント米財務長官がイランから殺害の脅迫を受け、最近、首都ワシントンの自宅から米軍基地に転居した。事情に詳しい関係者２人が１０日明らかにした。

米紙ニューヨーク・タイムズが最初に報じた。ロイターが１０月下旬に確認したメモによると、トランプ政権の情報機関高官は、米政府関係者や米国民を狙うイランの計画がかなり進展していると警告していた。

ベセント氏は８月以降、イランに船舶への攻撃停止とホルムズ海峡の再開放を迫るため、「オペレーション・エコノミック・アウトキャスト」と名付けた米国の制裁・経済圧力作戦を主導している。海上輸送の要衝である同海峡は、米国とイスラエルが２月２８日にイランを攻撃して以来、ほぼ閉鎖された状態が続いている。

経済圧力作戦は米海軍によるイランの港湾封鎖と並行して実施されており、イランとの取引を支援する中東の銀行支店やその他の金融サービス会社への制裁が含まれる。

米財務省の報道官は電子メールで寄せた声明で「長官はイラン政権の脅迫にひるむことなく、オペレーション・エコノミック・アウトキャストの遂行と封鎖の維持に引き続き全力を尽くす。両措置が相まってイラン経済を崩壊させつつある」と表明した。

ニューヨーク・タイムズは、ベセント氏への脅迫がどの程度深刻なのかは現時点では不明だと報じた。

事情に詳しい関係者によると、米紙ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナルがベセント氏のジョージタウン地区の邸宅を上空から撮影した写真を掲載したことで、同氏の身辺警護を巡る懸念が強まった。ベセント氏は２０２５年１月に財務長官への就任が承認された直後、この邸宅を１２５０万ドルで購入していた。

同関係者は、写真から自宅の所在地を特定できるようになったため、安全確保に向けてベセント氏を軍基地に移したと説明。「公職者への脅威が高まる中、報道機関には責任ある行動を取る義務がある」と述べた。

イランはこれまで、米国内で当局者や一般市民への攻撃を計画しているとの疑惑を否定している。

ニューヨーク・タイムズによると、米当局者は、イランが米国をはじめとする国外で大規模な攻撃を実行する能力は限られていると指摘している。

item.title: ＮＢＡ＝八村、チームトップタイの13得点 クリッパーズ敗れる
item.description: ［１０日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１０日　ロイター］ - 米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）は１０日、各地で試合を行い、八村塁が所属するクリッパーズはサンズに１１０─１３３で敗れ、今季８敗目となった。

先発した八村は約２３分間のプレーでチームトップタイの１３得点５リバウンドを挙げたほか、１アシスト２スチール。ほかにダリアス・ガーランドとババ・ミラーが１３得点を挙げた。サンズはジョーダン・グッドウィンが両チームトップの１８得点を挙げるなどし、最大で３２点のリードを奪った。

ニックスはバックスに１１７─８５で快勝し、４連勝。カールアンソニー・タウンズが２１得点１６リバウンドの活躍を見せ、開幕から１０試合連続、昨季から数えると１４試合連続でのダブルダブルを記録した。ジェイレン・ブランソンが両チーム最多の２３得点で貢献した。

一方のバックスは７連敗。開幕から１勝１０敗という数字は１９９３─９４シーズン以来で、１０敗中８試合は１０点差以上をつけられての黒星となっている。

セルティックスはセブンティシクサーズに１２３─１０１で勝利し、４連勝。ポール・ジョージが両チーム最多の３６得点、ジェイソン・テイタムが２１得点で続き、第２クオーター以降は一度もリードを奪われなかった。シクサーズはタイリース・マクシーがチームトップの２４得点を挙げたが、及ばなかった。

三井化学、今期純利益を530億円に上方修正　ナフサ高騰で 11/11 13:50 配信

[東京 １１日 ロイター] - 三井化学は１１日、２０２７年３月期の連結純利益予想（国際会計基準）を４５０億円から５３０億円（前年比５４．２％増）に引き上げると発表した。ナフサなどの原料価格上昇に伴う価格改定で交易条件が改善したことが主因。

・ＩＢＥＳがまとめたアナリスト１１人の予想平均値は５７９億円だった。

・営業利益も従来の８３０億円から１１２０億円に引き上げ

写真はＥＮＥＯＳホールディングスのロゴ。2020年8月、都内で撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato（ロイター） Shiho Tanaka

[東京 １１日 ロイター] - ＥＮＥＯＳホールディングスは１１日、２０２７年３月期の連結純利益（国際会計基準）予想を従来の４１５０億円から６１５０億円に上方修正すると発表した。前年比２．３倍となる。原油価格の上昇と石油製品の海外市況が前回予想の前提を上回る水準で推移したため。

ＩＢＥＳがまとめたアナリスト６人の予想平均値４６３２億円を大幅に上回った。

事業別では、海外市況を捉えた輸出増などにより石油製品で前回予想比２３００億円の増益、原油・ガス価格の上昇により石油・天然ガス開発事業で同４００億円の増益を見込む。通期の営業利益予想は前回予想比３０００億円増の９１００億円に引き上げた。年間配当予想は前回予想の３４円から３８円に増額した。

２６年４─９月の連結純利益は前年比７．９倍の５１１９億円となった。原油価格の上昇と円安進行に加え、石油製品の輸出収益改善やＪＸ金属株式の追加売却益が寄与した。

一方、開発コストや金利上昇などを踏まえて投資方針を見直した結果、２０２２年のジャパン・リニューアブル・エナジー買収に伴い発生したのれん等を主因に再生可能エネルギー事業で１１１８億円の減損損失を計上した。

[リオデジャネイロ／サンパウロ １０日 ロイター] - ブラジルの国営石油会社ペトロブラスが１０日発表した第３・四半期決算は、純利益が前年同期比２１．５％増の３９７億レアル（７１億ドル）となったものの、アナリスト予想の４７０億レアルを下回った。

イラン戦争を受けてブラジル政府が導入した石油輸出税として支払われた４５億レアルが影響した。

ＥＢＩＴＤＡ（利払い・税引き・償却前利益）は８５８億レアルで、３４．３％増となったが、これもコンセンサス予想の９４０億レアルを下回った。

ペトロブラスは１５３億レアルの株主還元を発表。３四半期連続で石油生産記録を更新しており、２０２６年の生産見通しを引き上げたと述べた。

四半期資本支出は１７％近く増加し、６４億ドルに達したことを受け、同社は投資の指標となる年間資本支出見通しを４０億ドル以上上方修正。この増加はプロジェクト総コストの上昇を示すものではなく、主に為替レートの影響などが反映されたという。

今年１─９月の投資総額は１６８億ドルに達し、前年同期比で２０．２％増加した。

声明で「当社は独自のポートフォリオを構成する収益性の高い投資を加速させており、今後も成長と営業キャッシュフローを通じて価値を創出し続けていく」と述べた。

item.content:encoded:
米共和党重鎮、エヌビディアＣＥＯに辞任要求　中国スパイ疑惑で 11/11 13:07 配信

報道陣に話しかけるエヌビディアＣＥＯのジェンセン・フアン氏。2025年12月3日、米国ワシントンD.C.のキャピトル・ヒルで撮影。（ロイター） Kanishka Singh

[ワシントン １０日 ロイター] - 米共和党上院の重鎮で銀行委員会に所属するケビン・クレーマー議員は１０日、半導体大手エヌビディアのジェンスン・フアン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）に対し、中国政府のスパイと疑われる中国人実業家の女性との不倫関係が判明したことを受け辞任を要求した。

クレーマー氏は米政治専門サイトのポリティコに「恐喝される恐れが極めて大きい。エヌビディアの半導体のような機密性の高いものを扱う以上、彼は辞めるべきだと思う」と語った。

さらに、「彼がした最悪のことが、中国のスパイかもしれないこの女性との不倫だとしても、それだけで十分だ。他に何があるか分からないのだから。私にとっては、それが安全保障上のリスクだ」と述べた。

この問題を巡っては、米治安当局が中国の情報活動への協力者と疑っている女性実業家とフアン氏が不倫関係にあったと、米紙ニューヨーク・タイムズが報道。これを受け、エヌビディアの取締役会が同氏を調査している。

トランプ米大統領は９日、連邦捜査局（ＦＢＩ）もフアン氏と女性の不倫関係を調べていると明らかにした。一方、中国外務省はスパイ疑惑を「根拠がない」とし、「中傷だ」と反論している。

エヌビディアは、米国の国家安全保障が損なわれたり、企業秘密が漏えいしたりしたと考える理由は取締役会にはないと説明。フアン氏は社内調査への協力を約束しているという。同氏は従業員に対し、妻を裏切って不倫したことを認めたが、関係の詳細は明らかにしていない。

フアン氏はシリコンバレーでトランプ氏に最も近い人物の一人。過去２年間、トランプ政権の政策への支持を繰り返し表明してきた。エヌビディアが中国市場への先端半導体の販売を目指す中、ワシントンにも頻繁に足を運ぶようになった。

民主党は中国向け半導体輸出の規制強化を求めている。

トランプ氏は９日、フアン氏と話し、女性がスパイだとは全く知らなかったと説明されたと述べた。フアン氏を信じているとも語った。

英アストラゼネカ、米バイオ新興企業買収　ワクチン開発強化 11/11 12:48 配信

2021年3月22日、米国デラウェア州にあるアストラゼネカ北米本社ビルの外で撮影。REUTERS/Rachel Wisniewski（ロイター） [１０日 ロイター] - 英製薬大手アストラゼネカは、バイオテクノロジー新興企業の米オムニオースを買収し、その事業を自社の感染症部門に統合した。オムニオースが１０日、明らかにした。オムニオースは重篤な細菌感染症に対するワクチンを開発している。

• 買収の金銭的条件は非公表。

• 両社間の３年間の独占的共同研究を経て、今回の買収に至った。

• 買収によりアストラゼネカは、単一のプロセスで細菌ワクチンの構成要素を設計・構築するオムニオース独自のプラットフォームを入手し、ワクチン開発体制を強化する。

• アストラゼネカ感染症部門のシニアバイスプレジデント、ベンジャミン・ムティエ氏は「オムニオースのプラットフォームは、結合型ワクチンの設計における差別化されたアプローチで、重い細菌感染症に対する当社の新規ワクチン開発能力を強化する」と説明した。

• アストラゼネカは多様な医薬品群を持つが、市販ワクチン製品は限られている。同社の最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は成長に改めて重点を置いており、１８０件超の医薬品候補プロジェクトがその長期的な成長戦略を支えている。

• 同社は２０２４年に新型コロナウイルスワクチンの販売を打ち切り、現在は呼吸器合胞体ウイルス感染症予防薬「ベイフォータス」と経鼻インフルエンザワクチン「フルミスト」を提供している。

• また同社は、がんワクチンの開発にも取り組んでいる。

Top US business leaders, including Tesla chief Elon Musk, are expected to join President Donald Trump's delegation to China for next week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit , the South China Morning Post (SCMP) reported on Tuesday (Nov 10), although it said Nvidia chief Jensen Huang's attendance is uncertain. Huang had previously been in talks to join the delegation, but his participation is now in doubt, the report said, citing sources, amid a recent controversy that has prompted Nvidia's board to investigate whether he was the target of a foreign intelligence operation. The APEC summit is set for November 18-19 in the southern Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen.

米ＳＥＣ、26年度の執行措置は35年ぶり低水準　前年度から大幅減 11/11 12:41 配信

米証券取引委員会（ＳＥＣ）のロゴと米国国旗。2025年4月23日に撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic（ロイター） Chris Prentice

［ニューヨーク　１０日　ロイター］ - 米証券取引委員会（ＳＥＣ）は１０日発表した年次報告書で、２０２６会計年度（２５年１０月―２６年９月）に実施した執行措置が３４８件だったと明らかにした。ロイターがＳＥＣの公式サイトに掲載されたデータと比較したところ、件数としては１９９１年度以来、３５年ぶりの低水準だった。前年度の４５６件から大幅に減った。

２６年度にＳＥＣが科した制裁金などの救済措置の金額は計約１１億ドル。ロイターが比較したところ、インフレ調整前の金額ベースとしては０８年以来、１８年ぶりの低水準となった。うち民事制裁金が３億４３００万ドル、不正に得た利益の返還として命じた金額が計７億５２００万ドルだった。

野党民主党や消費者団体などは、トランプ政権の圧力でＳＥＣが執行を大幅に後退させていると批判している。今回の結果を受けて反発が高まりそうだ。

トランプ政権は、過度に厳しい法執行はビジネスを阻害し、上場企業の場合には株主を罰することになると一貫して主張してきた。トランプ氏に指名された規制緩和派のポール・アトキンスＳＥＣ委員長は、自身が就任する前のＳＥＣの動きは不透明で、予測不可能だと指摘している。

アトキンス氏は年次報告書で「ＳＥＣの執行プログラムの成功は、最終的にはＳＥＣが使命をいかに効果的に推進し、投資家を保護し、不正行為者に責任を問うとともに、市場への信頼を強めることができるかによって測られる」とした上で、「執行措置や金銭的救済措置は活動の重要な指標ではあるが、それらが唯一の指標であるわけでも、最も説得力のある指標であるわけでもない」と主張した。

今月３日投票の中間選挙で大勝した民主党は議会上下両院で過半数を奪還し、上院銀行委員会委員長には同党のエリザベス・ウォーレン議員（東部マサチューセッツ州選出）が就任する見通しだ。ウォーレン氏は、ＳＥＣの執行措置件数が大幅に減ったことについて「議会で過半数を占めることになる民主党は、アトキンス氏が率いるＳＥＣが米国民を保護しているのか、それとも詐欺師や（ニューヨークの金融街）ウォール街を拠点とするトランプ氏の仲間である億万長者らのために働いているのかを厳しく精査することになる」との声明を出した。

［シアトル　１０日　ロイター］ - 米航空機大手ボーイングが１０日発表した１０月の航空機納入は４９機で、前月の５７機から１４％減少した。前年同月は５３機だった。

ただ受注はキャンセル調整後で、１０月としては１９９７年以来最高を記録した。キャンセルはゼロで、新規受注は１６５機。その大半は、航空機リース大手アボロンから受注した「７３７ＭＡＸ」１４０機。

• １０月に納入した７３７ＭＡＸは３２機で、９月の４３機から減少した。ケリー・オートバーグ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は先月、今年の７３７型機の納入目標である約５００機を達成できないとの見通しを示していた。

• 納入機にはこのほか、「７８７ドリームライナー」１１機、「７７７」貨物機２機、「７６７」３機が含まれる。うち１機は防衛部門ボーイング・ディフェンスのＫＣ－４６給油機プログラム向け。

• ボーイングは７３７型機の生産を月産４７機に引き上げる取り組みを進めているが、納入機数は減少した。オートバーグ氏は２０２７年初頭にこの生産ペースに達するとの見通しを示している。

• ７３７型機の主翼生産が依然として制約要因となっているほか、サプライヤーとの問題により７７７型貨物機と７６７型機の主翼生産が停滞している。

• １─１０月の累計納入機数は５２４機で、前年同期の４９３機から約６％増えたものの、６２１機を納入した欧州の競合相手エアバスに大きく後れを取っている。

• ニュージーランド航空はエコノミークラス向けの簡易寝台「スカイレスト」について、欧州規制当局による認証を待っている途中だが、７８７型機２機を受領した。

• １０月の受注のうち１５０機が７３７ＭＡＸ。内訳はアボロン向け１４０機、米格安航空会社（ＬＣＣ）アレジアント・エア向け６機、未公表顧客向け４機。残りの１５機は未公表顧客向けの７８７型機。

The Republicans will be the minority party in both chambers of Congress during the final two years of Trump's presidency.

WASHINGTON: Republicans chose US Senate Majority Leader John Thune and House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan on Tuesday (Nov 10) to lead them against a Democratic-controlled Congress that will take power in January for the final two years of Donald Trump's presidency. A week after Republicans lost their majority in a stinging midterm election defeat, Senate Republicans chose Thune by acclamation at a closed-door meeting for the task of trying to thwart Democratic initiatives that do not meet with their approval, including by wielding the Senate filibuster. "We're not going to be running this place next year," Thune told reporters. "But you can be assured we will be very, very active in asserting conservative priorities in all of the legislating ... that goes on here." Jordan's election as House minority leader elevates a combative Trump ally to the forefront of the party’s fight to defend the US president’s agenda in the lower chamber. Jordan defeated House Majority Leader Steve Scalise in a secret ballot. House Speaker Mike Johnson opted not to stand for the leadership position.

US Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-South Dakota) speaks at a press conference on the day of the Senate Republican caucus leadership elections at the US Capitol in Washington, DC, on Nov 10, 2026. (File photo: Reuters/Elizabeth Frantz)

The House and Senate leadership elections will help to determine what role Republicans intend to play as the minority party in Congress during the final two years of Trump's presidency. Democrats will need Republican support to move major initiatives in the 100-member Senate, where the filibuster rule requires 60 votes for most legislation. Their majorities in both chambers also fall well short of the two-thirds of votes needed to override presidential vetoes. Thune, 65, a South Dakota Republican known for his consensus-building leadership style, is respected by Republicans and Democrats alike. But he has run afoul of Trump's MAGA supporters who say he did not move aggressively enough to enact Trump's policies on immigration and election reform. After the midterm elections, Thune vowed that Republicans would work with Trump to block "Democrat extremism" and work against any attempt by Democrats to unwind Republican achievements, including border security and judicial appointments. Jordan, 62, was first elected in 2006 to represent a deeply conservative rural district in northern Ohio and was a founder of the House Freedom Caucus, a group that former Republican House Speaker John Boehner labelled "legislative terrorists". Before entering politics, Jordan honed his pugilistic style during a career as a high school and university champion wrestler, and later as a wrestling coach at Ohio State University. That past threatened his political career in 2018 when former students accused him of turning a blind eye to rampant sexual abuse of college wrestlers by the wrestling team's doctor, when Jordan was an assistant coach. Jordan denied all allegations, and a university investigation found no hard evidence that he knew of the abuse. But former wrestlers said the doctor's abuse was well-known and the report itself found that students had complained about the doctor's voyeurism in front of coaching staff. Jordan has often referred to his wrestling background in terms of his reputation as a fighter in Congress. He is known for his aggressive style of questioning in committee hearings. "I look at it like a wrestling match," Jordan told the New York Times in an April 2023 interview, explaining how he prepares for hearings. "I'm going to try to get as ready as I can. You can't just wing it."

By Joshua McElwee BUENOS AIRES, Argentina, Nov 10 (Reuters) – Pope Leo drew a crowd of a million on Tuesday for the third strong turnout of his 12-day South America tour, as he urged young people at a nighttime vigil in Argentina not to be consumed by the pursuit of money or social media popularity.

Throngs stretched for miles down the Avenida del Libertador, one of Buenos Aires’ main boulevards. Many waved cell phones, screens shining in the black night, as Leo was driven slowly through the crowd in an open-air popemobile.

Chants of “This is the pope’s youth!” rang out as the vehicle stopped frequently so security officials could bring forward babies for Leo to bless.

Show Full Article

In a speech, the pope warned young people against worship of modern-day “idols” such as success or physical appearance, and lamented that some youth “go so far as to lie, betray or humiliate someone on social media.”

“Do not bow down before anything that cannot give you life,” he said.

Leo, on an ambitious three-country tour through November 17, led the vigil after returning from a day trip to Cordoba, Argentina’s second city, where he drew 650,000 people to an outdoor Mass earlier on Tuesday.

The pope led a Mass on Monday at the Avenida del Libertador that drew 2.5 million people, in the largest event of his 18-month-old papacy.

POPE SEEKS TO SHORE UP CATHOLIC STRONGHOLD

Leo is the first pope to visit Catholic-majority Argentina since 1987.

The pope, who is also visiting Uruguay and Peru on the tour, is seeking to reinforce a region that has long been a Catholic stronghold but where the Church has been losing ground to fast-growing evangelical denominations.

Leo has emerged as a forceful voice on the world stage, lamenting what he sees as a failure of global leadership. In Argentina, he has directly challenged President Javier Milei, a libertarian and close ally of US President Donald Trump.

On Sunday, Leo urged Milei, who has pushed an austerity agenda that the Church has criticized for cutting social services, not to target Argentina’s poorest. Milei has said spending cuts were necessary to bring inflation under control.

Valentin Gomez, 21, a student attending the Mass in Cordoba, praised Leo’s focus on those in need.

“In these difficult times we are living through, he is greatly needed,” Gomez said. “Someone who is truly concerned about the poor.”

Cordoba Cardinal Angel Sixto Rossi, a critic of the austerity policies, welcomed Leo’s visit as a chance for the pope to see how Argentina is suffering under Milei’s measures.

“He knows how beautiful our people are and the ugly part, the leadership of the government,” he said in an interview with Argentine media. “He doesn’t arrive blindfolded.”

Argentine Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno said Cordoba was chosen as a stop on the pope’s tour because of its location in the center of Argentina, allowing pilgrims to travel easily from neighboring provinces.

Leo, the first US-born pope, spent decades as a missionary in Peru. The Vatican has described the trip, one of the most demanding foreign tours by a pope in decades, as a “homecoming” for him.

(Reporting by Joshua McElwee, additional reporting by Leila Miller, Lucila Sigal, Horacio Soria; editing by Chizu Nomiyama, Rod Nickel and Stephen Coates)

FAST

WASHINGTON: Republicans in the US House of Representatives blocked an effort on Tuesday (Nov 10) to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, winning a reprieve for the polarising Pentagon chief before Democrats take control of Congress next year and possibly try again. The vote on a procedural motion came just hours after Hegseth blasted efforts to impeach him as a farce and delivered a defiant defence of his record at the helm of the US military, winning praise from President Donald Trump. The chamber voted 211 to 204 in favour of a motion to refer eight articles of impeachment to the Republican-led House Judiciary Committee, a move that the sponsor of the impeachment push, US Representative Thomas Massie, warned would kill it. Massie, an outgoing Kentucky Republican, had hoped to draw votes from Republicans upset with Hegseth's policies and wary of the unpopularity of the eight-month-old Iran war but no other Republicans joined him. The US-Israeli led conflict has never been approved by Congress, which is the only branch of government constitutionally permitted to declare war.

Democrats had voiced strong support for the impeachment articles, which accuse Hegseth of the "high crimes and misdemeanours" of illegally ordering the military to wage war in Iran and Yemen, attack boats in the Caribbean Sea and capture Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in January. But 11 Democrats, including former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi of California, did not vote. If eight of them had, the procedural measure would have been defeated, paving the way for a full House impeachment vote. Ian Krager, a spokesperson for Pelosi, said she had missed the vote because she had returned to San Francisco for an annual event to honour veterans, but would have voted against the procedural measure. Trump cheered the results in a social media post, saying the effort to impeach Hegseth "has miserably FAILED!" He wrote that Hegseth's performance on Iran, Venezuela and other issues "led to the EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot." Hegseth would have been the first US defence secretary to be impeached. The last time any civilian leader of the US military was impeached was in 1876, when William Belknap held the title "secretary of war". Hegseth calls himself secretary of war, part of his effort to rebrand a military he said was too weak and "woke" when he took office last year. Trump cannot change the name of the Defense Department without approval from Congress.

IRAN WAR ANGER Voter anger over the Iran war, which has settled into an effective stalemate focused on securing the Strait of Hormuz, helped Democrats win control of Congress in last week's midterm elections. A Reuters/Ipsos poll published on Tuesday found a majority of Americans want the newly elected Democratic-majority US Congress, which takes office in January, to act to end the war with Iran once and for all. Although Vice President JD Vance has publicly questioned the war and blamed it for the Republicans' midterm rout, he voiced support for Hegseth on Tuesday. "This isn't about Iran, this is about the fact that Pete took on the bureaucracy at the Pentagon," Vance wrote on social media. Before the vote, House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Monday: "Pete Hegseth has abused his power, undermined America's national security, and he's the architect of the reckless and costly failed war of choice in Iran." Hegseth has repeatedly defended the conflict, calling Trump courageous and saying Iran's military has been left in ruins. He also said his orders to US forces were lawful, despite Massie's accusations of "high crimes and misdemeanours". "History will judge the Iran war quite differently than the conventional wisdom right now," Hegseth said on Tuesday at his first Pentagon briefing in six months. Jeffries said he would talk to members about whether to mount a new impeachment effort in the next Congress. "We'll have that conversation at the appropriate time," he said. A Democratic-led push to impeach Hegseth could be far more intense, with lawmakers calling in top brass to testify, including generals and admirals fired by Hegseth who have remained silent so far. Hegseth, who has railed against diversity efforts at the Pentagon, fired the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, who is Black, and the Navy's top admiral, a woman, among others. In such an effort, Democrats could also raise other issues of concern to voters including Pentagon policy toward Ukraine and the US military's strikes on suspected drug trafficking boats in Caribbean and Pacific waters. Some Republicans say Hegseth's strained relations with Congress are becoming a political liability as the Trump administration seeks a huge increase in the military's budget to US$1.5 trillion from US$950 billion. Massie said he was disappointed by the vote, comparing Republicans to passengers content to go down with the Titanic. "They know it's a sinking ship but committed to stay on board," he said.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog urged lawmakers to "do everything to avoid another election”.

JERUSALEM: Israel 's parliament was sworn in on Tuesday (Nov 10) without a new government , after a deadlocked general election stripped Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his parliamentary majority but left his main rivals with no clear path to power. Lawmakers elected in the Oct 27 vote took their oaths of office as Gadi Eisenkot , a former general, sought to forge a coalition after Israel 's president tasked him on Sunday with forming a government . Eisenkot and his allies also lack a majority and he has yet to strike deals with parties that could bring him to power. If both Eisenkot and Netanyahu fail to form coalitions, another election could follow. Presiding over the swearing-in ceremony, President Isaac Herzog told lawmakers: "You must do everything to avoid a repeat election."

"Reach out a hand for compromise, even between rivals ... Look upon one another with generosity. There is much work to be done here, and it requires the ability and experience found in every part of this House."

PARLIAMENT COULD TRY TO SET UP OCT 7 INQUIRY Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister until a new candidate manages to form a coalition. His right-wing Likud party's alliance with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties outperformed election expectations but still lost its majority, now holding 53 of the Knesset's 120 seats. Eisenkot's centre-right Yashar party and patchwork partner factions hold just 48 seats. But they have potential allies in Israel 's Arab-led parties, which hold 19 seats and are aligned with Eisenkot in their vehement opposition to Netanyahu . This means that the newly sworn-in parliament could still deliver on some of Eisenkot's campaign promises, such as potentially setting up a commission of inquiry into the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas attacks, something backed by the Arab parties but largely opposed by Netanyahu . It also could allow Eisenkot to replace the current Knesset speaker, a Likud member. Herzog told Knesset members that parliament was "duty bound to leave no stone unturned" in investigating and understanding the "catastrophe" of Oct 7, while Israel continues to face threats from Iran and its proxies. Eisenkot initially has until Dec 6 to form a government but he can seek a two-week extension to Dec 20. He has acknowledged his path to power is "extraordinarily complex". His options include trying to form a minority government with Arab party support, bringing ultra-Orthodox parties into his camp despite years of mutual hostility, or forging a unity government with Netanyahu . All three paths face formidable obstacles. Ultra-Orthodox parties have so far said they would not join an Eisenkot-led government .

For his part, Netanyahu has cast doubt on the election results by baselessly alleging voter fraud by Arabs, who make up a fifth of the population. Election officials have said they are probing potential misconduct, but that they have seen no evidence of fraud that could have influenced the vote's outcome. Speaking after parliament was sworn in, Netanyahu called for a unity government , warning that Iran was seeking to revive its nuclear programme and that Israel could come under growing international pressure to accept a nuclear-armed Iran. "Only such a (unity) government will be capable of confronting challenges of this magnitude," he said. If Eisenkot fails to form a government , Herzog would likely ask Netanyahu to try to build a coalition. If he also fails, another candidate would get a chance before Israel would be forced into another election. Moments after the official opening of parliament, Eisenkot and his allies submitted a series of bills, including legislation to establish a state commission of inquiry into the Oct 7 attacks and to impose term limits on the prime minister. They also proposed repealing a controversial judicial overhaul and other laws enacted under Netanyahu 's government over the past four years. Among those sworn in on Tuesday was Elisha Madan, a military reservist who lost both legs fighting in Gaza. He received a standing ovation from lawmakers as he rose on his prosthetic legs to take the oath of office.

item.content:encoded: Gold prices fell nearly 3% on Tuesday after hotter-than-expected US inflation data lifted the dollar and Treasury yields while reinforcing expectations of a bigger interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve this year. Spot gold XAU= was down 2.8% at $4,021.36 per ounce by 11:33 a.m. ET (1635 GMT). US gold futures GCcv1 for December delivery fell 1.9% to $4,036.00 per ounce. “I think it’s a bit of a short-term negative for gold because the inflation numbers were running a little higher than expected,” said Edward Meir, an analyst at Marex. The US Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% last month after advancing 0.6% in September, the Labor Department’s Bureau of Labor Statistics said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a 0.3% month-on-month rise. Bets on a 50-basis-point Fed rate hike in December started to build after the inflation print and comments by Fed governor Christopher Waller, who said he would support more aggressive action in the event of a too-hot Consumer Price Index report. The probability of a 25 bp hike is fully priced in, while the possibility of a 50 bp hike rose to 10.5% from 0% before the data, according to CME’s FedWatch Tool. The US dollar .DXY rose against a basket of other major currencies, and Treasury yields climbed. A stronger dollar makes gold more expensive for overseas buyers, while higher Treasury yields increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion. “(Gold) continues to trade above the critical $4,000/oz mark,” Standard Chartered said in a note, adding “crude oil, inflation risks and equity markets continue to set the tone of trading for gold with a focus on rate hike expectations for the December Fed meeting.” Meanwhile, the Monetary Authority of Singapore said it would launch a vaulting service to hold bullion for foreign central banks and lower taxes on some companies in the gold market as it competes for a bigger slice of the precious metals trade. Spot silver XAG= fell 3.9% to $51.32 per ounce and palladium XPD= was down 2.0% at $1,021.22. (Reporting by Vedika Thorat and Anjana Anil in Bengaluru; Editing by Kirsten Donovan and Jonathan Ananda)
